family_history: No family history of Alzheimer's or Parkinson's

social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife; three adult children

patient.chief_complaint: Slow progressive gait problems, daytime incontinence, and difficulty remembering recent events — admitted for evaluation
patient.history_present_illness: A 69-year-old retired high school principal with hypertension and well-controlled obstructive sleep apnea (CPAP-compliant) was admitted following referral from his primary care physician for a two-year history of progressive gait difficulty, urinary incontinence, and cognitive decline. He first noticed gait problems two years ago while trying to walk quickly to catch a bus — he found he could not move his legs fast enough and had to abandon the attempt. Over the subsequent months his walking progressively slowed and he began to take shorter steps. His wife noticed a 'magnetic quality' to his gait. He has had three falls — two in the kitchen and one on a garden path — none causing significant injury. He now avoids uneven surfaces and has limited his walking to short distances inside the house. Urinary incontinence began approximately 18 months ago. He describes strong urgency and insufficient time to reach the bathroom, resulting in accidents approximately twice per week. He initially attributed this to rushing and drinking too much coffee, but reducing his fluid intake had no effect. His wife notes he repeats himself in conversation, frequently cannot recall what was said 5 minutes prior, and has difficulty planning a dinner party they used to host effortlessly. Neuropsychological testing ordered by his primary care physician 4 months ago showed executive dysfunction and processing speed impairment. Head CT at that time showed enlarged ventricles with Evans index estimated at 0.36. He was referred for formal NPH workup and admitted for MRI and tap trial.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, fully oriented. MoCA 23/30. Mild delayed recall deficits (2/5). Executive dysfunction on Trail Making B (not completed). Processing speed reduced. No aphasia. Good insight into his deficits.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. PERRL. Extraocular movements full. No papilledema.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal tone and strength throughout. No rigidity. No resting tremor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Normal throughout including vibration, proprioception, and light touch.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, magnetic gait with short steps and reduced step height. Moderate shuffling. TUG 24 seconds. 10-meter walk 18 seconds. Cannot tandem walk. Pull test — 2 steps backward.
neurological_exam.additional: Bilateral grasp reflexes present. No nuchal rigidity.

mri.impression: Clear iNPH findings: Evans index 0.36, callosal angle 78°, DESH pattern, periventricular transependymal signal, prominent aqueductal flow void. Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to cortical atrophy. Clinical correlation recommended.

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 16 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 40 mg/dL. Glucose: 68 mg/dL (ratio 0.72). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 778 pg/mL (normal). total_tau: 202 pg/mL (normal).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (38 mL) with quantitative gait analysis
specialized_test.impression: Clearly positive tap trial — 33% TUG and walk improvement, 3-point MoCA improvement. All Hakim's triad components respond. Excellent VP shunt candidate.
recommended_actions: Neurosurgery referral for VP shunt placement

output.query: obstructive sleep apnea cognitive impairment differentiation from NPH

results.title: OSA and cognitive impairment — reversibility with CPAP
results.key_finding: OSA-related cognitive impairment improves with CPAP therapy; CPAP-compliant patient with persistent cognitive decline has an alternative neurological cause

output.summary: This patient is CPAP-compliant with adequate OSA control (confirmed by CPAP download showing AHI <5/h). His cognitive decline persists despite good OSA treatment. OSA is NOT the cause of his cognitive impairment — NPH is the primary diagnosis.

output.impression: Negative amyloid PET. No concurrent Alzheimer's pathology. Excellent prognosis for cognitive recovery with VP shunting.
Hyperdynamic aqueductal flow — peak velocity 20 cm/s, stroke volume 72 mcL/cycle. Both above normal range. Consistent with iNPH pathophysiology.
Frontal-subcortical improvement pattern consistent with iNPH. Executive function and processing speed most responsive — hallmark features for VP shunt candidacy.

findings.finding: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity — involuntary contractions at 145 mL. No outlet obstruction.

output.impression: NDO consistent with NPH frontal lobe dysfunction. Expected to improve post-shunting.

findings.finding: CPAP usage 6.8 hours/night average (95th percentile of nights ≥4h: 98%). AHI on therapy: 2.8 events/hour. Adequate OSA control.

output.impression: Excellent CPAP compliance with adequate OSA control. Residual AHI 2.8/h (target <5/h achieved). Cognitive impairment is NOT attributable to undertreated OSA. NPH remains the primary diagnosis.
